📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Pokemon Winds & Waves leaker has admitted to faking rumors about the Gen 10 games, giving fans fresh hope for voice acting and Eevee’s first latest evolution in more than a decade.

Sources indicate that moot, who posts as @Mootmonthly on X, had built a reputation for sharing information about the Pokemon anime. Centro Leaks had publicly vouched for him as a reliable anime source, and his claims about an internal delay for Winds & Waves made it into Dexerto’s November 9 coverage.

Meanwhile, a separate account called @kurwashibamaste had been feeding Centro Leaks rumors about the games since July. It claimed a development build appeared to lack fresh evolutions for Eevee and Tropius. It also claimed voice acting had been planned but had disappeared from recent builds.

According to recent reports, on November 17, an X user posted a screenshot appearing to show Moot and @kurwashibamaste in the same account switcher. Moot responded with a GIF captioned “How it feels to spread misinformation and lies.” Centro then said Moot had admitted to running the alternate account and faking many of its Winds & Waves rumors.

Some drama on the Pokémon leak community happening:– @Mootmonthly has admitted to faking a lot of the rumors he started regarding Winds/Waves– Has admitted to being behind the @kurwashibamaste from which a lot of rumors went viral last few months– We now think most of the….

Moot later mentioned he had accomplished a “specific goal” with the account and described keeping up the act as a “larp.” He also said his reputation had made him feel limited in what he could post and that he’d “prefer being viewed as a clown.”.

Sources indicate that also honestly? my rep was a little too goodthe dexerto article was neat but having that level of rep kinda forces one into being rather limited in what they can say/posti vastly would prefer being viewed as a clown.

The reveal frustrated fans who had spent months following the rumors. Pokemon creator Light remarked he had gotten it wrong himself and criticized other accounts for allegedly staying quiet when they suspected what was happening.

Pokemon Winds and Waves reportedly had 2026 launch planned before last-minute delay.

Pokemon Winds and Waves leak reveals map and first look at Grass Gym.

AI Pokemon Winds & Waves “leaks” are fooling fans ahead of Gen 10.

Others were happy to see those rumors fall apart. Pokemon creator SoulSilverArt said a Tropius evolution, a upcoming Eeveelution, and voice acting were “back on the menu.” Eevee’s last new evolution was Sylveon, which debuted in Pokemon X and Y in 2013.

Well there’s some real confirmation, Moot is Kurawashi…Looks Tropius Evo, latest Eeveelutions, and VA ARE BACK ON THE MENU BOYS! https://t.co/4chqJMxX6G pic.twitter.com/45M3tN4Yi7.

Centro noted some real details may have been mixed in. It pointed to the rumor of around 300 new Pokemon and forms as one it had heard separately, adding that development prepares could have changed.

The Pokemon Tech giant has yet to announce voice acting or a new Eevee evolution. It has confirmed a 2027 release on Nintendo Switch 2 and revealed Gen 10 starters Browt, Pombon, and Gecqua.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A free Christian parody of Grand Theft Auto is launching alongside GTA 6, and getting five stars will bring Satan after you instead of the cops.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A free Christian parody of Grand Theft Auto is launching alongside GTA 6, and getting five stars will bring Satan after you instead of the cops.

Sources indicate that with players finally jumping into Vice City, satire site The Babylon Bee is opening up a city of its own. The game is called Grand Faith Auto, and it takes place in New Mercy, a 3D open world you can explore right in your browser.

The setup will look familiar to anyone who’s played GTA, as there are cars to take, storefronts and billboards dotted around the city, and a radar to help you find your way.

But while the real thing often throws you into the criminal underworld, Grand Faith Auto is all about being an upstanding citizen.

Recent findings suggest that instead of the traditional Wanted level, doing good deeds earns you stars of divine approval. Get all five, and the devil himself comes looking for you instead of the cops.

Industry observers note that one of the deeds you can do around New Mercy is pull a driver out of their car and preach to them before driving off in it yourself. You can also offer a “Lady of the Night” a lift to church, or try to feed the hungry in a scenario involving a closed chicken restaurant, a deli under attack, and a box of pocket Bibles.

There’s even a stealth mission where you sneak into a cartel warehouse and swap its drugs for little figurines. You’ll have to stay out of sight, because getting spotted by a guard is an instant fail.

Sources indicate that the official Grand Faith Auto game launch trailer. It's the upcoming hit video game everyone's been waiting to play for years. Available November 18!Grand Faith Auto is free, while Grand Theft Auto VI will cost your eternal soul (plus $80).Just go to https://t.co/21fFFTXowv pic.twitter.com/aBJRRtTeZY.

You’re not completely unarmed, though, as you can wield a holy shotgun to fend off the imps tracking you down. A shot to the head stuns them, leaving you free to kick them back to hell. After that, the instructions tell you to go to church.

Police can’t wait for GTA 6 to be released so they can “catch a break”.

GTA 6 forces you to take your time with the main story instead of speedrunning it.

GTA 6 best guides for launch: Everything you need to know.

Discussing the game in an X post, The Baylon Bee CEO Seth Dillon said that he doesn’t expect the game to actually rival GTA 6, it’s just a “Christian alternative.”.

That’s probably for the best, given that GTA 6 has already become the joint-best-reviewed game of all time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hershey’s is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day only to celebrate the theatrical release of its new movie, giving customers several ways to take advantage of the promotion.
  • The chocolate company is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.
  • The promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hershey’s is bringing back its original five-cent chocolate bar price for one day only to celebrate the theatrical release of its new movie, giving customers several ways to take advantage of the promotion.

The chocolate company is celebrating the November 25 debut of Hershey, a biographical film exploring the lives of Milton Hershey and his wife, Catherine “Kitty” Hershey, with a limited-time deal inspired by the brand’s history.

The promotion will allow customers to purchase classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bars for just a nickel, matching their original price from 1900. However, the process for claiming the discount varies depending on where customers shop.

The promotion will take place on Wednesday, November 25, with discounted chocolate bars available through Hershey’s Chocolate World, Walmart, and Amazon Grocery.

Customers visiting Hershey’s Chocolate World locations in Hershey, Pennsylvania, or Times Square in Newly introduced York City can purchase the bars for five cents each beginning at 9 AM local time.

Industry observers note that there is a limit of 10 bars per person, and the offer cannot be combined with other discounts. Applicable taxes will still be charged.

Walmart customers can also take advantage of the promotion through two different methods. Those shopping online can purchase a classic Hershey’s Milk Chocolate Bar for five cents by placing an online pickup order through Walmart.com using their Walmart account.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, customers shopping at Walmart stores can receive the discounted price through the Ibotta app. After purchasing a qualifying chocolate bar, shoppers must upload a photo of their receipt to receive cash back.

Walmart’s promotion is limited to five bars per person and does not apply to orders shipped directly to customers’ homes.

Chipotle releases hoodie designed to sneak burritos into movie theaters.

7 Brew adds food to its menu for the first time with five new $3 treats.

Reese’s adds bizarre warning to Halloween candy after $5 million lawsuit.

Amazon Grocery will also participate in the promotion, offering five-cent chocolate bars through same-day delivery in select markets.

In a recent development, customers with qualifying delivery addresses can use a promotional code shared through Hershey’s social media channels to receive free shipping at checkout. The offer is limited to two bars per customer while supplies last, with taxes calculated based on the total order.

“The five-cent bar gives fans a chance to experience a sweet piece of Hershey’s story for themselves,” the company stated in a statement shared with PEOPLE.

“Bringing it back on the day HERSHEY debuts in theaters gives fans a fun way to celebrate the brand’s roots and the story that inspired it.”.

Alongside the promotion, Hershey’s is introducing vintage-inspired packaging for several products, including its Milk Chocolate Bars and Kisses chocolates.

Industry observers note that the packaging features the company’s historic wordmark, Milton Hershey’s signature, and typography inspired by the brand’s early years. Each package also includes a QR code directing customers to more information about Hershey’s history.

The upcoming movie stars Finn Wittrock as Milton Hershey and Alexandra Daddario as Catherine Hershey, following their relationship and the development of the chocolate company.

Directed by Mark Waters and filmed in Pennsylvania, the movie also features Alan Ruck, David Costabile, Richard Kind, and several other cast members.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar has cut longtime ways to hook up with other characters in GTA 6, including hiring sex workers, as it builds the game’s romance around Jason and Lucia.

GTA 3 let players pay for sex back in 2001, and later games gave them more ways to pursue other characters. San Andreas gave CJ six potential girlfriends, while GTA 4 let Niko Bellic meet dates through the in-game internet.

GTA 5 kept paid hookups and gave players another option at the Vanilla Unicorn strip club. Flirting with certain dancers during a private dance could lead to leaving the club with them, hooking up, and calling them again later.

GTA 6 still puts Jason in suggestive situations in the main story with side characters attempting to seduce him, and strangers around Leonida flirt with him openly and invite him into explicit situations. But unlike GTA games from before, that’s as intimate as Jason is allowed to get.

Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier remarked a trip to the strip club was the closest he found to a way to cheat on Lucia, and he later confirmed you cannot kiss anyone except your partner.

You can't kiss anyone except your partner.

Sources indicate that the Guardian’s review confirmed that either lead can get a private dance on their own or the couple can go together. Shacknews confirmed that players can no longer pick up sex workers.

Industry observers note that rockstar described Jason and Lucia as “a couple in a bind, lovers on the run” in a statement to Shacknews. The studio stated it chose which features to bring forward based on how they fit the story and the gameplay systems it wanted to expand.

GTA 6 is giving players more freedom to complete missions their own way.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An Arizona judge ordered YouTuber Lane Myers released from prison after county prosecutors raised doubts about an email that helped send him there.

Sources indicate that myers, 43, pleaded guilty in July 2025 to felony stalking and harassment charges involving Shannon Walker, the wife of Tucson city prosecutor Matthew Walker. He was placed on probation under conditions that restricted what he could post about the couple.

Sources indicate that in October 2026, Pima County Superior Court Judge Douglas Metcalf sentenced Myers to three years in prison for violating that probation. Prosecutors said Myers had posted upcoming YouTube videos about the Walkers and argued those videos prompted others to send Shannon Walker threatening and harassing emails.

It has been revealed that investigators tied at least one of those emails to an IP address associated with the Walkers’ home, casting doubt on whether the message came from someone reacting to Myers’ videos. Who sent it remains under investigation.

Deputy County Attorney Rachel Stiles submitted the new evidence under seal and discussed it only in broad terms at the November 17 hearing.

Tucson police searched the Walkers’ home on November 2 and seized several devices, including Matthew Walker’s city-issued laptop. County prosecutors first asked for Myers’ release at an emergency hearing the next day. On November 5, the city of Tucson put Matthew Walker on paid administrative leave while police investigated possible misconduct connected to the probation case.

A Tucson YouTuber was ordered freed from prison after county prosecutors found evidence suggesting the victim or her husband, a city prosecutor, may have drafted harassing emails that helped put him behind bars. https://t.co/An6DVVsuFD.

Metcalf returned Myers to probation on November 17, and his 2025 stalking and harassment convictions still stand. Myers thanked county prosecutors in a statement for bringing the evidence forward, and thanked Metcalf for “giving me the opportunity to show I can follow conditions.”.

It has been revealed that stiles said county prosecutors still believe Myers violated his probation and will review the evidence before deciding whether to ask the court to revoke it again. Metcalf scheduled a status hearing for December 8.

Burger King is bringing a massive burger inspired by the Grand Theft Auto franchise into the real world, introducing a seven-patty Whopper based on a fictional fast-food restaurant featured in the games.

The latest creation, called the HeartWhopper, is part of a limited-time promotion from Burger King Belgium that allows GTA fans to win a real version of the oversized burger.

The campaign introduces on November 19 and takes inspiration from the fictional fast-food chain found throughout the GTA series, turning one of its recognizable menu items into an actual meal.

The HeartWhopper features seven flame-grilled beef patties stacked with cheese, tomato slices, lettuce, and onion rings, recreating the exaggerated burgers associated with the fictional restaurant.

According to Burger King, the promotion is intended as a parody of the video game franchise’s own parody of fast-food chains, with the firm claiming its restaurants have served as inspiration for fictional businesses in gaming.

Rather than introducing the HeartWhopper as a traditional menu item, Burger King Belgium is giving players the chance to win one through a social media competition.

A post shared by Burger King BE & LUX (@burgerkingbe).

To participate, fans must share a video clip showing themselves enjoying a burger from the in-game restaurant and tag either Burger King Belgium or Burger King Luxembourg.

In a recent development, the company will select the most creative submission each day, awarding the winner a real-life HeartWhopper. The competition will run for two weeks, giving players multiple opportunities to participate.

Burger King is also promoting the campaign through YouTube advertisements, YouTube Shorts, and gaming communities on Reddit, with teasers released ahead of the November 19 launch.

Tech Report: Building the next generation of multimodal AI experiences with fal in Microsoft Foundry

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Video workloads do not all start with the same input or aim for the same result.
  • Recent findings suggest that today, Microsoft and fal are helping developers find the right tools for their workloads.
  • Sources indicate that the partnership expands the choices available in Microsoft Foundry while bringing video into the broader platform developers use to build AI applications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Video workloads do not all start with the same input or aim for the same result. A creative team might explore several interpretations of a written brief. A retailer might turn an approved product image into a short motion concept. An application developer might combine image generation and video generation into a workflow that takes an idea from description to frame to scene. Each scenario brings different requirements for visual quality, motion, creative control, turnaround time, and cost. All of this means that a multi-model solution is necessary to realize a full vision.

Recent findings suggest that today, Microsoft and fal are helping developers find the right tools for their workloads. We are excited to announce that Kling, LTX, and MiniMax video models are rolling out to in public preview in Microsoft Foundry through our newly introduced partnership with fal. Available as a first-party Azure service, these text-to-video and image-to-video options give creators and developers more ways to utilize video generation with the experiences they want to build.

Sources indicate that the partnership expands the choices available in Microsoft Foundry while bringing video into the broader platform developers use to build AI applications. The goal is to let developers pick the right model for each step of an experience, then connect those steps into a working application.

“fal has seen incredible adoption this year alone with generative media across all industries from advertising to marketing to gaming. Partnering with Microsoft allows both of us to truly enable the wide creative ecosystem and ensure that all AI solutions that lean on generative media, becomes a multi-model one.” - Burkay Gur, Cofounder.

fal is the full stack for generative media, built for creators and developers, with APIs for over 1500 models across image, video, audio, 3D, and generative worlds. As a truly encapsulating platform, fal provides inference, training, and infrastructure to run generative media workloads in production, while also providing innovative post trained models that pushes the boundaries on speed and quality.

In a recent development, that specialization matters because generative media is both a creative and an engineering workload. A compelling demo is only the start. Production applications also need to handle real traffic, scale with demand, and balance output quality, latency, and cost.

In a recent development, through this partnership, developers will be able to access a selected set of video models in Microsoft Foundry, served by fal and sourced from the companies that build them. The initial portfolio gives teams a choice of models for different creative requirements instead of relying on one model for every task, with more models planned over time.

Industry observers note that the initial portfolio spans Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo. These models give developers different starting points for generating video from text and animating existing images. A team rapidly exploring creative concepts may prioritize speed and cost, while a team producing fewer, higher-fidelity assets may weigh output quality more heavily. Whether an application starts from text or an existing image, and what it needs in output quality and cost, also shapes the choice.

Kling: From a still image to a directed scene.

In a recent development, kling v3 Pro combines cinematic visuals and fluid motion with native audio generation and custom element support. Its image-to-video capabilities give developers control over how a starting image becomes a moving scene, a fit for applications that prioritize visual direction and motion.

LTX: One model for fast drafts, one for final output.

In a recent development, for rapid iteration and previews, LTX-2.5 Fast is the speed-optimized option; for high-fidelity final output, LTX-2.5 Pro is the quality-optimized option. Both support text-to-video and image-to-video generation with synchronized audio.

MiniMax: Another approach to video generation.

In a recent development, miniMax H3 Max and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo are post-trained variants of MiniMax H3 focused on prompt adherence, aesthetics, and inference performance. For developers, they provide additional options to evaluate against an application’s creative brief, quality requirements, and performance needs.

“When building with video models, the details matter: how closely the output follows your prompt, how well it preserves your reference images/videos/audios and how swiftly you can try another idea. Kling gives developers control over detailed reference to video generation. LTX offers fast iteration and high-quality output through its Fast and Pro variants. H3 Max brings fal's post-training and inference optimizations to improve quality and speed. Having these models available through Microsoft Foundry gives developers more flexibility to choose what works best for the application they are building." - Gökay Aydoğan, Creative Engineer.

Bringing video generation into an enterprise application requires more than choosing the right model. Teams need a platform where they can evaluate different options, build with the models that fit their requirements, and operate those experiences alongside the rest of their applications.

In a recent development, the initial portfolio of video models is hosted in the US, and Microsoft Foundry is the first provider to offer a US-hosted Kling 3 endpoint. Key considerations for enterprise teams:.

In a recent development, video generation pricing varies by model and output resolution, giving teams options to balance creative requirements with their application’s budget. The table below shows pricing in USD per minute of generated video for LTX and MiniMax models, making it easier to compare costs across the available options.

Pricing will be updated and listed on our Azure pricing page within the coming weeks.

Ready to start building? Join us at Ignite for BRK256: Video AI at Scale with fal on Microsoft Foundry. Naomi Moneypenny and Alexander Hughes from Microsoft will be joined by Burkay Gur and Lovis Odin from fal on stage to explore this partnership on Thursday, November 19 at 11:00 AM - 11:45 AM CT. Register today!

Explore Kling v3 Pro, LTX-2.5 Fast, LTX-2.5 Pro, MiniMax H3 Max, and MiniMax H3 Max Turbo in Microsoft Foundry and find the model that fits your video experience.

How Applicant Tracking Systems Read Resumes: 7 Checks Developers Should Make

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Recent findings suggest that 7 Day Free Trial.
  • According to recent reports, A resume that looks perfect on screen can look like a pile of scrambled text to a program.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Sources indicate that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

Recent findings suggest that 7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

According to recent reports, A resume that looks perfect on screen can look like a pile of scrambled text to a program. Applicant tracking systems (ATS) and hiring tools do not see your layout. They extract text from a file, guess where the sections are, and store what they find. If that step fails, the best experience in the world never reaches a human reader.

This matters whether you are sending your own resume or building a tool that processes thousands of them. This article walks through seven checks you can make with a few lines of Python, including one script you can run today.

A resume is a document with no guaranteed structure. One person writes "Work History", another writes "Experience", and a third uses a two-column layout that reads out of order. Any tool that processes resumes first has to turn this into predictable fields: contact details, sections, dates and skills.

Thinking in terms of a target schema helps. SitePoint's article on JSON schema design for document AI indicates how the structure of the labels you define determines whether a document pipeline works. The same idea applies here: decide which fields you need before you write any extraction code.

According to recent reports, do not judge a resume by how it looks. Judge it by what comes out when you extract the text. SitePoint's walkthrough on building a JSON dataset from PDF documents describes a pipeline that extracts text from PDFs and then cleans up common extraction artifacts. That cleanup step exists because raw extraction is rarely tidy. Read the raw output first, and note what is broken.

PDF files store where characters are placed on a page, not what they mean. The pypdf documentation on extracting text from a PDF says this directly: there is no semantic layer, spacing is hard to get right because text is absolutely positioned, and pypdf is not OCR software, so it will never extract text from images.

In a recent development, two practical results follow. A resume saved as a scanned image has no extractable text at all. And fancy layouts such as columns, text boxes and tables can come out in the wrong order.

It has been revealed that once you can extract text, a short script can catch the common failures. This one reads a PDF and reports whether it contains text, whether an email address is found, and which standard sections are missing:.

Run it on a resume and look at the result. If has_text is false, the file is probably an image. If sections are missing, check whether your headings use unusual names. A passing result does not prove that every ATS will read the file the same way, but a failing result is a clear warning.

Recent findings suggest that different tools parse differently, so one script is only one opinion. A resume writing service such as ResumeCroc lists a free ATS resume checker among its tools, which is a quick way to see how another tool reads the same file. The linked page is a commercial service page, and every ATS behaves differently, so treat any checker as one data point and compare it with your own extraction results.

Sources indicate that most extraction problems come from layout. Single-column pages, standard headings, plain fonts and real text instead of images give parsers the best chance. Avoid putting contact details in headers or footers, since some tools skip them. If you are building a parser, test files with columns and tables on purpose so you know how your tool fails.

Create a folder of sample resumes: a clean one, a two-column one, a scanned one and one with unusual headings. Run your check against all of them whenever you change your parsing code. This turns "it seems to work" into something you can verify, and it makes regressions obvious.

Do all applicant tracking systems read PDFs the same way? No. Parsers differ in how they handle layout, headers and tables, so test more than one file format and more than one tool.

Is a Word file safer than a PDF? Not necessarily. Both can parse well or badly depending on layout. Test your own file instead of assuming.

Recent findings suggest that can a script guarantee my resume will pass an ATS? No. A script can find obvious problems, such as missing text or headings, but each hiring tool has its own rules.

According to recent reports, hiring tools read text, not layout. Define the fields you care about, extract the raw text first, understand what PDF extraction cannot do, automate basic checks, compare with an outside checker, keep formatting simple, and test against a small set of sample files. The script above is short, but it moves the question from "does it look right" to "what does a program actually see".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players in Japan have voiced disappointment over the game’s censored content, which tones down nudity and gore compared with the Western release.

Japan is no stranger when it comes to censoring video games, with recent examples like Resident Evil Requiem famously featuring black textures over decapitated body parts and less blood.

However, on November 10, it was revealed that the Japanese version of GTA 6 was 1 GB smaller than its overseas brother. This quickly sparked fears among players that the game would be missing content to make it pass Japan’s ratings board. Well, it turns out that those fears were indeed true.

It has been revealed that A screenshot of protagonist Jason taking a shower in the Japanese version of the game has gone viral, and no, it’s not because he’s getting all soapy. Rather, it’s because he’s showering in what can only be described as a tiny black Speedo.

For contrast, the overseas release has Jason showering in his birthday suit, with there being no steam or swimwear to obstruct his bare buttocks from view. As you can imagine, many fans aren’t exactly happy with these watered-down scenes.

“Isn’t it strange that in a country where people go completely naked in public baths and hot springs, they make people wear swimsuits to take a shower?” wrote one Japanese player.

“If they’re going out of their way to give it a CERO Z rating for 18+, what’s the point of censoring the content? I don’t get it,” replied another commenter.

日本の表現規制のクソっぷりが全世界に知れ渡ってめちゃくちゃ気分が良いもっと燃やせ https://t.co/xphLiZCi2C.

Nudity isn’t the only thing that has been toned down, as Japanese gaming website Game*Spark found that the Japanese version has no option to adjust the intensity of blood and gore.

GTA 6 fans fear censored content as file size is smaller in certain regions.

GTA 6 almost banned in Korea after government officials got to play it early.

According to recent reports, can GTA 6 download codes be seen through sealed boxes? Warning goes viral days before launch.

According to recent reports, this is in comparison to the overseas version that comes with three adjustable settings, which allow players to tweak how much of a bloody mess they want to see when shooting at NPCs. The Japanese version also has less blood left on the ground after gunfights, although dismemberment remains in the Japanese release.

“They could just use parental controls and the like to restrict content that’s harmful to children, but instead, decent adults get content shoved at them that’s been watered down to the point of having its teeth pulled,” added another angry fan.

GTA 6 was released on November 19 and is now the joint best-reviewed game of all time, sitting alongside The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A high school in Pennsylvania has been forced to scrap a test of AI-powered metal detectors after regular student items were continually flagged as weapons.

In a recent development, over the last few years, a number of places have updated their security systems, scrapping old metal detectors in favor of newer ones – you’ll have seen them at airports, for example. These up-to-date detectors are supposed to speed up the security process, but they can cause headaches.

That has been the case for the Hempfield Area High School in Pennsylvania, as they have been helping to test the new Wi-AI detection system from CurvePoint AI.

As per TechSpot, Wi-AI uses Wi-Fi signals to look for concealed weapons, with people having to walk near SensePods, which tracks movements without even using cameras.

However, according to WTAE-TV in Pittsburgh, everyday items that students need for school – including binders, water bottles, and batteries – have been routinely flagged as weapons.

It has been revealed that “The detection is not what they were hoping to get from the technology side of things and so, we are in agreement that, moving forward, as far as going live, its just not a product that is ready for that activation,” Superintendent Dr. Mark Holtzman told the news outlet.

Skip Smith, the CEO of CurvePoint AI, noted that the school “served as a testing and evaluation site” rather than being a full “operational deployment.”.

Additionally, Holtzman noted that the system was “not near” the 95% accuracy rate that the system hoped to achieve.

It has been revealed that it isn’t the first time that similar systems have caused these sorts of headaches. Back in October 2025, a 16-year-old student in Baltimore was swarmed by armed police when an AI gun detection system falsely flagged a Doritos bag as a firearm. That system was shut down just a month later, too.

The long-awaited sequel arrived on November 19 to rave reviews, after racking up well over $1 billion in pre-orders, and is likely to be one of, if not the biggest, video game releases ever.

GTA 5 sold more than 230 million copies, and Rockstar animation programmer Nestor Uriarte says the follow-up is expected to surpass it.

But for some of the people who made it, launch week also brings questions about what happens in the weeks and months that follow.

According to recent reports, uriarte, who works at Rockstar’s Edinburgh studio, raised those concerns in an opinion piece for The Guardian. He described the pressure game developers have come to expect on either side of a major launch.

“While the highs of a game release like this can be incredible, game workers have also come to expect other, less welcome side effects: intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath,” Uriarte wrote.

He pointed to job losses across the games industry to explain why those fears persist, even at Rockstar.

Sources indicate that “It claims a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.”.

It has been revealed that as a result, Uriarte said he was voting in favor of union recognition because he wants staff to have a say in pay, bonuses, and working conditions. He said Rockstar has already introduced some overtime pay and wants to build on that so workers are paid for every hour they put in.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A latest law from the European Union could impact the way ads from influencers and pay-to-win items in games work, especially those that target minors.

Recent findings suggest that back on November 10, the European Union laid out its first proposal for what they’re calling the Digital Fairness Act. In short, the DFA is looking to clamp down on “unfair commercial practices” that are regularly seen online.

The European Union highlighted things such as “manipulative marketing tactics or hidden fees” as targets of the bill, but they’re also looking at advertisements from influencers too.

It has been revealed that while influencers are at the moment required to use hashtags like ad, sponsored, and gifted on their content, the Digital Fairness Act wants to strengthen that. “Clear disclosure of influencer marketing, requiring influencers to be transparent about commercial content and preventing the exploitation of the trust of minors in their audience,” the EU pointed out as one of the “key” parts of the proposal.

Additionally, pay-to-win and pay-to-progress items in games have also been highlighted as part of the latest act.

Recent findings suggest that “Fairness by design, with the option for consumers to turn off addictive design features that encourage excessive or compulsive spending, such as persistent prompts. The proposal will also restrict unfair practices that encourage overspending, for example by banning gambling-like features for minors, such as pay-to-win and pay-to-progress,” they added.

It’s unclear as to how broad that anti-pay-to-win protection would be, seeing as there are continual arguments about what can be classified as P2W.

There would also be a crackdown on “fake claims” that tell people to rush to buy items due to apparent low stock and changing prices.

In the United States, a number of ticket resale websites have sued the District of Columbia over a upcoming law that will cap the resale price of tickets at 10% above face value.

#35256. Breaking: AI Testing Tools: Benefits, Limitations, and Best Practices

📅 29 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (728 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sitepoint ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: AI Testing Tools: Benefits, Limitations, and Best Practices

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (728 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • Recent findings suggest that every vendor notes the same thing: buy our AI, and testing gets easy.
  • They support your QA team by writing test cases, running them, spotting failures and suggesting repairs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

It has been revealed that weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

Recent findings suggest that every vendor notes the same thing: buy our AI, and testing gets easy. Don't believe it. AI testing tools do help, though. Some teams save real hours with them, while others waste a quarter and a budget. The difference usually comes down to how they start.

They support your QA team by writing test cases, running them, spotting failures and suggesting repairs. Some tools read a requirements document. Others watch real users click around and then replay what they did. Playwright, for instance, now ships built-in test agents: a planner that explores your app and writes a test blueprint, a generator that turns the plan into test files, and a healer that runs the suite and tries to repair failing tests.

According to recent reports, old-school automation needs a person to write every script. Then a developer moves one button and the whole thing falls over. Somebody loses a morning to repairs, and QA engineers hate that part of the job.

Quality is the big worry. Generated tests can look clever and prove nothing. A tool might confirm that a checkout page opens and then mark checkout as covered, but opening a page is not testing it. Even Playwright's documentation says generated tests may contain initial errors and that you should review what the healer changes before accepting it. A person has to read the output every time.

Business logic is the next problem. The tool has no idea that your refund window dropped from 30 days to 14, and it cannot feel that a signup form is confusing. Intent lives in people's heads.

Recent findings suggest that coverage numbers can mislead. A dashboard claims 90%, and the room relaxes. Meanwhile, the odd edge cases nobody thought of sit untouched. Bugs do not read dashboards.

Recent findings suggest that check fit first. Does it cover web, mobile and API tests, and does it work with your stack? Ask before any sales call, not after. Then test its honesty: when something fails, a good tool tells you why. A vague red mark costs your team time because nobody can verify it. Read the pricing page slowly, too, since some vendors charge per seat and some per test run.

Finally, throw your ugliest feature at it. Demos use tidy little apps, but your product has pop-ups, slow pages and odd corners. Watch how the tool handles those.

Expecting instant results. People switch the tool on and wait for magic. What they get is noisy reports and grumpy engineers. Some managers even cut QA headcount right away, which is a bad idea: somebody has to tune the tool and handle the cases it cannot. Good testers become more valuable, not less.

Skipping training. Your team needs to learn how the tool behaves. Two short workshops and a shared doc go a long way.

Trusting machine-written text without a second look. AI tools now draft test descriptions, bug reports and release notes too. If your team wants to know how much of a document was machine-generated, an AI-content checker such as ZeroGPT can give a rough signal. Treat the result as a hint rather than proof, because such detectors make mistakes and publish their own accuracy claims.

Sources indicate that agents are the obvious next step. Instead of running fixed scripts, they poke around your app like a curious user, clicking, typing and reporting anything strange. Early versions already exist, and they are rough but improving.

Industry observers note that editors will change as well. Your code editor may soon suggest a test the moment you finish a function, and some bug reports may arrive with a fix attached. The wall between development and QA is getting thin.

Industry observers note that yes, but carefully. AI testing tools will not replace your QA team. They take the boring work off testers' hands and spot patterns people might miss, but they still need a human to say "that result is wrong." Start small, measure what happens and keep your testers close to the tool. Do that, and you will ship faster without losing control.

Testing JSON-LD Like an API: 7 Checks Before Your Next Release

📅 29 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1040 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sitepoint

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.
  • A content editor changes an article’s headline.
  • Neither failure necessarily produces a JavaScript error.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stay up to date with AI tools, model releases, and developer workflows that matter.

Weekly. Free. One click to leave.

7 Day Free Trial. Cancel Anytime.

A content editor changes an article’s headline. The page updates immediately, but its JSON-LD still contains the previous title. A redesign introduces a fresh author component while an old plugin continues publishing a different author name in the page source.

Neither failure necessarily produces a JavaScript error. Both leave machines and readers with conflicting descriptions of the same page.

For developers, the useful approach is to treat JSON-LD as a maintained output of the application, with a data source, validation rules, and regression tests. This guide uses a blog template to show how. You will need basic JavaScript knowledge and a modern Node.js installation for the runnable tests.

In a recent development, requests for search improvements often arrive as broad outcomes: improve discoverability, clarify entities, or support answer engines. These need to become implementation requirements before development starts.

For example, AEO directory includes structured data within descriptions of broader optimization services. For an engineering team, the actionable deliverable is a page representation whose types, properties, and values can be checked against the published content. I personally used this , and adding this because this can help other developer's and designer for optimization and get higher search result's.

For a blog template, define these acceptance criteria:.

Keep implementation success separate from search outcomes. Google’s AI features guidance indicates there is no special Schema.org markup required for its AI search features. Correct markup also does not guarantee rich results or inclusion in an AI-generated answer.

According to recent reports, avoid separate, manually maintained copies of the headline, author, and publication date. Both the visible template and metadata builder should consume the same published record.

Save the following as article-schema.mjs. The builder assumes an upstream content-validation step has already checked required strings, timestamps, and approved HTTPS URLs.

In a recent development, this is a deliberately small example, not a complete rich-result eligibility checklist. Add relevant images and other supported properties when the real page supplies them. Consult the Schema.org BlogPosting definition and Google’s Article documentation for their respective vocabularies and search guidance.

Use a consistent canonical-URL policy before building the identifier: normalize the intended hostname, trailing-slash convention, and query parameters. Do not generate a fresh UUID for the same article on every request.

SitePoint’s guide to implementing JSON-LD on modern websites covers embedding approaches across common stacks.

Valid JSON is not automatically safe to insert into a raw HTML script element.

A CMS value containing can terminate the element at the HTML-parser level, even when the value belongs to a JSON string. Concatenating a headline directly into a script tag is particularly risky.

Append this helper to article-schema.mjs:.

JSON serialization handles quotes and backslashes. Replacing literal less-than characters prevents an embedded closing-script sequence from appearing in the resulting text. The Next.js JSON-LD guide documents this approach for script embedding.

Use the serialized result as the content of a script element with type="application/ld+json". Follow your framework’s documented embedding mechanism so the JSON is neither double-encoded nor inserted through an unrelated HTML context.

In a recent development, this helper is specific to JSON-LD script content. It is not a general-purpose HTML sanitizer, URL validator, or substitute for validating CMS data.

The tests should catch changes that would make metadata misleading or unsafe, not merely confirm that an object exists.

Save this file as article-schema.test.mjs beside the builder:.

Recent findings suggest that these are unit tests for the builder and serializer. They do not prove that a template embeds the script correctly or that the deployed page is eligible for a search feature. SitePoint’s explanation of unit, functional, and integration testing helps distinguish those responsibilities.

A passing builder test cannot detect a page component reading a different CMS field.

According to recent reports, add a browser-level check against a controlled article fixture. Inspect its visible heading, byline, dates, canonical link, and JSON-LD together. For this template, assert that the intended article entity appears once and matches those visible fields.

In a recent development, do not assert that the entire page contains exactly one JSON-LD script. A site may legitimately publish organization, breadcrumb, and article entities separately. Instead, identify the relevant entity by its @id and detect conflicting definitions.

Include these failure cases in the test proposal:.

Prefer generating metadata from the content loaded during server rendering or static generation when that fits the application. If it is injected client-side, inspect the rendered result and test navigation explicitly. Avoid making essential metadata depend on a user interaction.

No single tool establishes syntax, semantic accuracy, search eligibility, and content consistency at once.

Use a small set of complementary checks:.

Test both representative code samples and deployed URLs. A validator cannot confirm the truth of an author name simply because the property is syntactically valid.

Sources indicate that google’s general structured-data guidelines also require markup to represent the page accurately. Treat validation warnings as findings to investigate; do not add invented reviews, dates, or attributes merely to improve a tool’s output.

Ownership matters after the first release. Decide which application layer generates article markup, who maintains its mapping, and which publishing events invalidate cached output.

In a recent development, when an editor changes a headline, the visible page and JSON-LD should be rebuilt or refreshed together. Updating one while serving the other from an older cache creates a mismatch even if both implementations are individually correct.

According to recent reports, avoid setting dateModified to the current time on every deployment. A CSS update or infrastructure rebuild does not necessarily mean the article changed. Read the timestamp from the editorial record instead.

Recent findings suggest that before shipping a template change, run the builder tests, inspect one rendered page per affected template, and check representative deployed URLs. Keep a small fixture set that includes optional fields, long text, translated content, and script-like strings.

According to recent reports, A reliable JSON-LD implementation has a traceable relationship with published content. When someone changes the page, its machine-readable description should change predictably—and the test suite should expose the cases where it does not.

A restaurant in North Carolina has hit out at “miserable and entitled” customers after their rules about tipping went viral on social media, and people thought that the answer would be to review bomb them.

Tipping in restaurants and bar has long been a divisive topic, with different places handling it in their own unique ways. Some establishments put an automatic gratuity charge on bills, while others still leave it up to the customer.

On November 15, the Freeman’s Grub & Pub in Greensboro, North Carolina, come under fire on the EndTipping subreddit after one user flagged a notice about their tipping rules.

In a recent development, “If our employees have two separate instances of you not tipping well without explanation, we will add a 20% autograt fee on your bill,” the rules state. “Your receipts will be saved if this is the case, and you are welcome to question it,” they also noted, urging customers to leave a name and number if they have any complaints.

The restaurant’s co-owner, Kevin Purcell, responded to the backlash on November 16, noting that he had been hit with review bombs online.

Recent findings suggest that “It is 2026, and you should know by now the rules of engagement and expectations to tip at a bar or restaurant. Our staff is beyond competent; they’re professionals at what they do. You’re expected to tip for the great to excellent service that they provide,” Purcell said.

“Servers everywhere talk s*it when you leave about how pathetic it is that you still don’t know the very basic rules of dining out at this point in your miserable and entitled existence.”.

Restaurant blasts customers for “stealing” over viral dine-and-dash videos.

Customer removes 15% automatic tip after server refuses to give him tap water.

Customer removes automatic 18% tip added to their bill and people are furious.

Purcell added that if there are genuine mistakes, then the restaurants does assist on that front, but they “take pride in providing a top-tier dining experience.”.

He noted that the restaurant will “stand behind our controversial policy and amazing staff,” despite what may come.

The response has garnered plenty of sympathy and fightback from customers who want to support the restaurant too. “I have never been to your restaurant but will go soon,” one said.

Recent findings suggest that “Just left a review! You guys are the best, it’s great seeing restaurant owners truly care about their staff” another commented. “Thank you for being an exemplary business,” another added.

GTA 6 screenshot hidden in San Andreas back in 2021 was real and the house has a dark secret

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (525 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dexerto

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A mysterious GTA 6 screenshot discovered in San Andreas Definitive Edition back in 2021 has finally been found in Rockstar’s upcoming game, confirming a theory that predates even the infamous 2022 hack.
  • Five years ago, players exploring GTA Trilogy: The Definitive Edition noticed something unusual inside the Lil’ Probe’Inn, a UFO-themed bar in San Andreas.
  • It has been revealed that among the photographs on the wall was a picture of a suburban house with palm trees and a UFO flying overhead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mysterious GTA 6 screenshot discovered in San Andreas Definitive Edition back in 2021 has finally been found in Rockstar’s upcoming game, confirming a theory that predates even the infamous 2022 hack.

Five years ago, players exploring GTA Trilogy: The Definitive Edition noticed something unusual inside the Lil’ Probe’Inn, a UFO-themed bar in San Andreas.

It has been revealed that among the photographs on the wall was a picture of a suburban house with palm trees and a UFO flying overhead. Unlike the other images, which came from existing Rockstar titles, nobody could identify where it was from.

Dexerto reported on the discovery in November 2021, with fans theorizing that Rockstar had secretly included the first-ever GTA 6 screenshot.

Now, with GTA 6 finally here, it turns out they were right.

The same day the game was released in Upcoming Zealand, a player named Jared from the GTA 6 mapping community discovered the house in Belville, located in Leonida’s Leonard County.

The building is almost identical to its 2021 appearance, right down to the garage, palm trees, and surrounding vegetation.

All credit goes to Jared from the GTA VI Mapping server.The house is located in Belville. (https://t.co/hWt1Koz3uz) pic.twitter.com/t2ZsSRPQFI.

However, players who break into the garage will discover something even more bizarre.

Inside is the hideout of a conspiracy theorist who has seemingly figured out that he’s living inside a video game.

Notes scattered around the garage reveal that the resident has been trying to escape Leonida, but can’t purchase a plane ticket to Los Santos or drive beyond the state’s borders. He’s even considering fleeing by boat.

The conspiracy theorist has also noticed NPCs who look identical, neighbors unable to enter their own homes, people glitching through walls, and buildings with nothing behind their locked doors.

GTA Trilogy players think they solved the ‘GTA 6’ house screenshot mystery.

First GTA 6 screenshot? GTA Trilogy players make significant discovery in San Andreas.

GTA Online insider says “leaked” GTA 6 screenshot mystery will finally be solved soon.

There’s even a graph showing an enormous spike in violent crime alongside numerous references to the number six.

The photo Rockstar added to GTA San Andreas Definitive Edition in 2021 was a real GTA 6 photo.You can visit that house to find more conspiracy theories hidden inside. pic.twitter.com/5vxNFBmsSQ.

It has been revealed that perhaps most interestingly, the resident identifies two individuals, known only as J and L, who appear immune to the strange limitations of his world. These are seemingly references to GTA 6 protagonists Jason and Lucia.

We’ll have to see if there’s even more to this discovery as players continue to explore Leonida and see everything the world has to offer.

The find is especially remarkable because the original screenshot surfaced in November 2021, nearly a year before the massive September 2022 Rockstar hack exposed early GTA 6 gameplay.

It’s unclear whether Rockstar planned the garage’s fourth-wall-breaking Easter egg all those years ago or added it after seeing the community obsess over the house.

Either way, the developer managed to hide a glimpse of GTA 6 in plain sight years before its official reveal.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

American Airlines has responded after passengers found that their bags had been covered in a brown, liquid-like substance while waiting two hours for them.

Sources indicate that when you get off a flight, there can be a sense of trepidation about what’s to come next. If you land at the wrong time, you’ll be stuck in a long security queue, meaning your bags might end up stuck on the reclaim belt or even taken somewhere else.

Recent findings suggest that well, for passengers on an American Airlines flight from Miami to Atlanta, they ended up having a two-hour wait for their bags after landing. Yet, that wasn’t the biggest glitch.

As TikToker Derick McCallum, who had been aboard the plane, noted, the bags ended up coming out looking like they’d been covered in poop. “Underneath the flight, it flooded. The doo-doo water got all in the bottom,” McCallum mentioned. “Now they’re bringing the bags out; there is doo-doo on the bags.”.

The TikToker’s video has racked up more than 1.3 million views, as of writing, with plenty of viewers commenting with their dismay at the claims.

However, an American Airlines spokesperson confirmed that it wasn’t feces on the bags, but rather liquefied peanut butter.

“Unfortunately, a food item from a customer’s checked bag leaked during the flight, affecting several bags nearby,” a spokesperson told the Upcoming York Post. “Our team will work directly with the affected customers to make it right.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 fans are discovering that driving while checking their in-game phone drastically changes the way their vehicle handles, spawning a wave of viral memes and videos that highlight how dangerous it is.

Driving while looking at your mobile phone is never a good idea, as it drastically impairs your ability to react to your surroundings and can even lead to fatal accidents.

Rockstar has also reflected the IRL challenges that come with doomscrolling while behind the wheel by having both Jason and Lucia’s driving skills take a complete nosedive.

In a recent development, just like GTA 5, players can whip out their phone while driving to check messages and interact with apps to their heart’s content. However, GTA 6 takes things a step further by making things even more dangerous. While Jason and Lucia’s smartphone doesn’t take up the entire screen, it does now block out more of your view.

This alone isn’t the only danger to any unfortunate NPC that happens to stray into your general direction, but the car also becomes noticeably harder to control. In fact, it feels like fighting with your controller when it comes to making those smooth maneuvers.

Recent findings suggest that as you can imagine, it’s not exactly the optimal way to drive, especially if you want to keep your car from becoming a total wreck or avoid any pedestrian-related accidents. Well, unless you’re after some run-ins with the cops (it is a GTA game after all).

Humilde aporte #uma #umamusume #GTAVI https://t.co/ZtbrLgIy9J pic.twitter.com/WhaCu9rePU.

However, in true GTA fashion, players have already turned the feature into a meme, editing Jason’s phone to show everything from Umamusume videos to scantily clad anime girls while he chaotically drives along a beach.

GTA 6 dev says Rockstar has to be “careful” with satire in newly introduced game.

GTA 6 makes huge change to iconic controls that might save controllers.

GTA 6 gameplay, map, radio, and cutscene leaked ahead of Netflix Extended Look.

One Tweet even showed Jason checking his Crypto, while Palworld’s Head of Publishing and Communications also joined in on the fun by uploading a video of the protagonist looking at its cat girl Sekhmet.

Hey this GTA game is pretty good pic.twitter.com/0MVIbQWNex.

“Generational memes will come from this game,” wrote one player. “You are doing the Lord’s work! Let the GTA 6 memes begin,” added another.

While GTA 6 has only been out since November 19, players are just getting started with the creative ways they can use the game’s smartphone to make memeworthy moments.
